<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a888c5c9ef31f138e4bec23cc8c88ab51641f4ae` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c4d9e7afb66c9dd6e89cc6fd0ef537d387d240b5` — the merge of head `4b30901d939959e40d65bfd457f3b93d5878efcf` into base `a888c5c9ef31f138e4bec23cc8c88ab51641f4ae`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c4d9e7afb66c9dd6e89cc6fd0ef537d387d240b5 && git checkout c4d9e7afb66c9dd6e89cc6fd0ef537d387d240b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a888c5c9ef31f138e4bec23cc8c88ab51641f4ae 4b30901d939959e40d65bfd457f3b93d5878efcf && git checkout -B drift-repro a888c5c9ef31f138e4bec23cc8c88ab51641f4ae && git merge --no-ff 4b30901d939959e40d65bfd457f3b93d5878efcf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a888c5c9ef31f138e4bec23cc8c88ab51641f4ae
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a888c5c9ef31f138e4bec23cc8c88ab51641f4ae` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `487a0f5bb8298be639a8c188039fd539c780dec7`
Local-runs: probe — the seat's brief ordered local runs on this head, in a detached worktree (removed, main checkout clean): the two pin files, one held ablation of the runtime export through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with the runtime rebuilt, a main leg (the three source files at the merge base's blobs, the runtime rebuilt), the ADR-0087 gate, `reviewFace`, and two uncommitted probe files (deleted): the door's answers by request and deployment shape beside the binder's own refusals, and the door over a runtime without the export
Scope: (no `hits` — narrowing face, no schema and no governed path) .changeset/32572-install-local-shared-job-name.md, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-jobs.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts (`collectBundleJobs`), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-rename-planner.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-package-registration.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/17/retry-policy-converged.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts (the `job` row), packages/types/src/env.ts (`resolveScheduledWorkEnabled`), packages/core/src/index.ts, .changeset/config.json, content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx

This is a complete ①–④ round on the PR's first head. There is no earlier contract-review record on this PR.

Read at 2026-11-12T23:20Z: card #32572, its two comments (claim 6836648648, dev report 6838155102), the seat's card brief, the PR body and the changeset at this head, the net diff against the merge base `5c0f1134` (6 files, +266 / −11), `git show --remerge-diff` of `487a0f5b` (empty; it brings #32804 and #32824, which touch neither package), the docs-drift comment 6838167668, and the head's check-runs (51: 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed; the last completed 2026-11-12T23:12Z).

**Result: PASS. No blocker; two should-fix (S1, S2) and three nits (N1, N2, N3), all prose or pins for one follow-up card.** The source is right: the door refuses by the binder's own function, over the list the binder reads, for the id the binder schedules under. Every pin holds, the dev's red and green counts reproduce, and an independent ablation through the built runtime reds both pin files. What is incomplete is the FROM → TO table, which the PR calls "every moved answer": two shapes of the same route move and no row names them (S1, S2).

Local runs on this head:

| Run | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`; `turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/cloud-connection^...' --filter='@objectstack/runtime...'` | exit 0; 38 tasks (20 cached) |
| The two pin files: `marketplace-install-local-jobs.test.ts` (23), `app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts` (64) | 23 / 23 and 64 / 64, exit 0 |
| The PR's two-minute command (`-t 32572` on the jobs file) | 6 passed, 17 skipped |
| Main leg: the three source files at `5c0f1134`'s blobs, the runtime rebuilt with its own `build` script (`collectJobNameCollisions` in neither built entry), the tests at head | cloud-connection 4 failed / 19 passed (the four refusal pins; both CONTROLs green); runtime 4 failed / 60 passed (the #32572 describe: `collectJobNameCollisions is not a function`). Restored: three blobs equal HEAD |
| Ablation, marker `CR32889_ABLATION`: the export's job list replaced by an empty one (`jobNameCollisions(bundle, appId, [] /* CR32889_ABLATION */)`, anchor hit 1, `--hold`); the runtime rebuilt; `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 2 built files | cloud-connection 4 failed / 23 (the same four), runtime 3 failed / 64 (the three arrangements); every CONTROL green. Restored: blob `2a0dcc813af1` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty; rebuilt, marker absent, export present (index.js 2, index.cjs 3) |
| The two pin files after the restore | 23 / 23 and 64 / 64 |
| `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base 5c0f1134` | exit 0; read as BREAKING, `!`, Clause-② narrowing, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` |
| `reviewFace` over the six paths, with the changeset and the PR body as carriers | `narrowing`, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, no hits |
| Probe A: the door's own harness shape (real runtime dist, recording job service, a `planUpgrade` and an importer stub), at head and on the main leg; for each arrangement the head's or main's `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` run on the same bundle | see ①, S1, S2, N1 |
| Probe B: the same door over a runtime module whose `collectJobNameCollisions` is absent (`vi.mock`), at head and on the main leg | see N2 |

A first spelling of the ablation (`return [] /* … */`) failed the runtime's DTS build on its unused parameters; it was restored (blob equals HEAD) before any test ran. The main leg and the ablated builds went through the package's own `build` script, not turbo, so no ablated artifact entered the turbo cache.

Not run here: the whole runtime and cloud-connection suites, the two typechecks, the 70 dispatch gates, lint and the dogfood battery. They are read from the dev report and the head's check-runs (Test Core 8 of 8, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset and Dogfood Regression Gate all success). Main is at `5fb79bc01`, five commits past the merge base; none touches either package's source (one `packages/core` test file), so the head was not merged with it here.

### ① Derived judgments

Probe A, the door's answers (scheduled work on unless named):

| Request | main leg | head |
|:--|:--|:--|
| install, one package, `jobs_app_twin` twice beside one job of its own name | 200, `hotLoaded`; one `error` line from the binder; only `jobs_app_other` scheduled (probe B, main leg) | 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR`; nothing registered, persisted or scheduled |
| upgrade, v1 [twin, other] then v2 [twin twice, other] | 200, ledger 0.2.0, `jobs_app_twin` cancelled, one `error` line | 422; v1 registered once, no further `schedule` call, nothing cancelled, both v1 jobs scheduled, ledger 0.1.0, no `error` line |
| `dryRun: true`, the twin package | 200 with the plan (`planUpgrade` called once) | 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `planUpgrade` not called |
| `dryRun: true`, distinct names | 200 with the plan | 200 with the plan |
| scheduled work off (the default), the twin package | 200, registered, nothing scheduled, one `info` line (declarative jobs not scheduled), no `error` line | 422, nothing registered |
| scheduled work off, upgrade v1 [twin] then v2 [twin twice] | 200, ledger 0.2.0 | 422, ledger 0.1.0 |
| scheduled work off, one handler-only job (the no-body precedent) | 422 | 422 |
| no `job` service, the twin package | 200, registered, one `warn` (job service not registered) | 422 |
| `installMode: 'unmanaged'`, the twin package, stub importer | importer called once | 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, importer not called |
| `installMode: 'unmanaged'`, one body job, stub importer | importer called once | importer called once |
| `kernel:ready` rehydrate of a ledger entry carrying the twin | not run (the diff does not touch the rehydrate) | registered, `jobs_app_other` scheduled, the twin refused at `error` |

Probe A, door against binder, the same bundle (scheduled work on):

| Arrangement | refusals the binder logs | main door | head door |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 one package, the twin beside a job of its own name | 1 | 200 | 422, quotes it |
| A2 one package, two names twice, and a disabled third of the first name | 2 | 200 | 422, quotes both |
| A3 one package, a twin whose second job is handler-only | 1 | 422 (no-body clause) | 422, quotes it, before the no-body clause |
| A4 two package bodies declare the name | 1 | 200 | 422, quotes it |
| A5 one body declares it twice (raw JSON; `defineStack` refuses this in one stack) | 1 | 200 | 422, quotes it |
| A6 the app's body and the residual, the residual running as that body | 1 | 200 | 422, quotes it |
| C1 distinct names, C2 a disabled twin, C3 both twins disabled | 0 | 200 | 200 |

"Quotes it" means the door's message contains, byte for byte, every sentence the binder logs after `NOT SCHEDULED — `, and the export names the same shared names.

- **Install and upgrade, scheduled work on: 200 → 422, before any write.** Right, and pinned. The upgrade leaves v1 whole: registered once, its jobs scheduled, nothing cancelled, its ledger entry kept. On `main` the same upgrade cancelled the installed job, which is what a 200 with a report would still do; the refusal is the only shape that keeps it.
- **Every holder shape: the bind refuses ⇔ the door refuses.** Measured over six refused arrangements and three CONTROLs, and by construction: `collectJobNameCollisions` is `jobNameCollisions` over `collectBundleJobs(bundle)`, the list the binder passes; the door passes `manifestId`, the id `bindArtifactHandlers` schedules under; the bind reads the body converted forward, and the one ADR-0087 conversion that maps `jobs` (`retry-policy-converged`) writes retry defaults only, never `name` or `enabled`. The run form does not move the answer: the name is judged before it, by the bind and now by the door (body and handler at the door here; pull through the runtime pin, whose three arrangements are pull jobs). No case was found where the door admits a name the bind refuses, or refuses one the bind schedules. The shapes where the bind judges no name at all are S2's.
- **Holder vocabulary.** The bind's message is quoted whole, so the door names every job by run form and every holder in the bind's words, the residual included (`this artifact's top level outside every package body (its residual, …)`). The runtime pin deep-equals the export with the logged refusals, `candidates` included (`{ kind: 'residual', ownerId }`). The door's answer carries no `details`, as the other 1d clauses carry none; the PR body gives the reason (a `details` would move `@objectstack/client`'s `err.details`).
- **A3 and the PR's row 4.** Already 422 on `main` by the no-body clause; the head adds the shared-name clause first. Right, pinned.
- **CONTROLs: distinct names, a disabled twin, both twins disabled.** 200 on both legs, nothing refused at bind. Pinned (two of the three).
- **The dry run, the default deployment, no job service, unmanaged.** See S1, S2 and N1.
- **The degrade path.** See N2.
- **The rehydrate is ungated.** An entry carrying the twin loads and the binder refuses the name, as on `main`. The ADR-0087 marker's reason rests on this, and it holds.
- **The dev's readings.** Head 23 / 23 and 64 / 64, red 4 failed / 19 passed on the cloud-connection file: reproduced (the red leg on the merge base's blobs, not `c04aa295`'s; the same four). The dev's door-side ablation and this record's runtime-side one red the same four door pins.
- **First-party reach: 0.** The one first-party job (`showcase_health_sweep`) has its own name, as #32563's census found.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cloud-connection: patch` and `@objectstack/runtime: patch`, title with `!`, a `**BREAKING**` paragraph with the remedy, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, `no-migration-prescription`), on the changeset and the PR body. The level is right: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its banner and disposition (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). The gate accepts it.

**The arm: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right.** The test is whether the card widens a published accept set or enlarges a public surface (the pm-dispatch execution duties, measured on the built entry). `collectJobNameCollisions` is a new name on `@objectstack/runtime`'s entry: present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`. Its parameters and return type reach `PackageScopedRefusal`, already public through `@objectstack/core` (`export * from './package-scoped-resolution.js'`), so the surface grows by one function and no type. The narrowing is the 200 → 422. The claim wrote `no (narrowing)` as "expected … to be measured", and the duties say the dev's measurement decides such a reading. `reviewFace` reads the narrowing face, whose comment names `yes (narrowing)` as one of its spellings.

**`Metadata-protocol: none` stands.** The rule (one enabled job name per artifact) has held at bind since #32563, which declared `Metadata-protocol: none` for the same refusal. `defineStack` already refuses a name twice in one stack's `jobs` (`StackCrossReferenceError`, met by probe A). No key, value or type moves; one door enforces an existing rule earlier.

**`Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx` is honest.** Its job-name paragraph still says a job of that name an earlier install scheduled is stopped. On `os package install` it now keeps running. Its install callout lists what `os package install` refuses without the shared name. `skills/**` teaches no install-door job refusal (grep). `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, which the docs-drift comment names, says nothing about job refusals. The doc half of S1 and S2 belongs on that card.

Size: +266 / −11 over 6 files. No governed surface and no `packages/spec` path.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no other login to name. The PR is a draft.
- File surface: `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` (+3) is outside the claim's named surface. It is declared in the dev report (out of scope, carrier the seat) and in the PR's Acceptance notes. It is the export's only route through the package entry. The deviation is small and necessary; the seat accepts or refuses it at ACCEPT.
- The `Clause-②:` line differs from the claim's expected value. The claim asked for the measurement, so this is no deviation (see ②).
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`: the seat files the jobs.mdx card and rewrites the line to `#N` before ACCEPT (the review checklist's rule).
- One merge of main (`5c0f1134`), before the PR; its remerge diff is empty. The branch is the platform-assigned one: not judged.
- `security_findings: none` in the dev report. Nothing security-relevant was found in this review; there is no private item.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the spec on `main`: ADR-0150 D3 says nothing picks one of several holders, and since #32563 the binder refuses a shared job name rather than keep the later job. The PR makes the install door refuse what the binder refuses, by the binder's own function, so that refusal is real at the door. It takes no declared capability away: `defineStack` already refused the single-stack shape, and jobs.mdx already says one artifact cannot hold two enabled jobs of one name.

- **Refuse, not report.** Right. It is how step 1d answers every job this door cannot run. On an upgrade it is the only answer that leaves the installed version's job running (measured on both legs).
- **Share, not copy.** Right. One exported function returning a type already public is the smallest widening that lets the door and the binder read one judgement. The binder still calls `jobNameCollisions` directly, and the export is a one-line view over it.
- **The package, not the deployment.** The door judges the package whatever the deployment's scheduled-work switch, as every 1d clause does: `main` already refuses a handler-only job on a deployment with the switch off (measured). That stance is consistent and a later switch-on and restart would meet the bind refusal, so it is not a defect. Its consequence on the default deployment is a move the text must state (S2).
- **No silent pick.** Every refused arrangement names every job and holder; nothing is scheduled by order. The degrade admits, and says so only in the log (N2), as the other two judgements do.

**S1 — should-fix, the follow-up card below. The dry run moves and no row names it.** `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` with `dryRun: true` (`os package install --dry-run`) on a twin package: `main` answered 200 with the upgrade plan; the head answers 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR` and reads no plan. Distinct names: 200 with the plan on both. The TO is right: the door's header says the dry run answers "after every refusal that says the package cannot install at all", and step 1d already refused a no-body job's dry run. The `Clause-②:` line covers it by route. But the PR's FROM → TO table ("every moved answer") has no dry-run row, the changeset's BREAKING bullets speak only of "the install", and no pin holds it. Fix: one row, one sentence in the changeset, one case in `marketplace-install-local-jobs.test.ts` (the harness needs only a `planUpgrade` on its `manifest` service).

**S2 — should-fix, the same card. The FROM is stated for a deployment that runs package-authored scheduled work.** The changeset's Before bullet says the binder "refused the name at `error`", and the PR's rows 1 and 2 say the same. That holds only with the scheduled-work switch on. The switch is off by default in every posture ("Unset means off", `packages/types/src/env.ts`). With it off, or with no `job` service, the binder judges no job name at all. Measured on `main`: 200, the package registered and ledgered, every job withheld (one `info` or `warn` line, nothing refused; with the switch off, no `error` line), and, with the switch off, an upgrade landed v2 whole. At the head: 422, nothing registered, and an upgrade is refused with v1's ledger entry kept. The move is declared (the route-level `Clause-②:` line and "Who moves" name every author whose package shares a name), and nothing in the text says a deployment is spared, so this is not a blocker. But on the default deployment the plain consequence differs from the one written: a package, or an upgrade, that installed whole (its jobs inert by the switch) is now refused whole, and no job of it was running to keep. Fix, prose: state the FROM by deployment shape (switch on: the bind refusal and the cancel; switch off or no job service: installed, jobs withheld, nothing refused), and say that the door judges the package whatever the switch, as it judges a job with no body. A pin for the switch-off install is optional.

**N1 — nit, prose, the same card. The unmanaged mode is listed as not changed, and its answer moves.** `installMode: 'unmanaged'` passes step 1d before the import, as the PR says. Measured with a stub importer: `main` reached the importer with the twin package, and the head refuses at 1d before it. With the real importer, any package carrying a job is refused `422 UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE` with `details.findings` naming `jobs`, since `job` is `allowRuntimeCreate: false` (read, not run). So for this mode the answer moves from one 422 to another (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, no `details`), not from 200. Two sentences are wrong for an unmanaged copy, which is never bound and has no earlier version: the `Clause-②:` line's "where it answered `200`", and the refusal's closing sentence ("Installed, … an earlier version … would be cancelled"). The other 1d clauses use the same managed-install wording. Fix: one row, and move the sentence out of "Not changed".

**N2 — nit, a pin and one sentence, the same card. The degrade path is declared in the PR body only, and is not pinned.** Measured with `collectJobNameCollisions` absent from the runtime module: the door answers exactly as `main` does. The install answers 200, the binder refuses the name at `error`, and only the other job is scheduled; an upgrade answers 200 and cancels the installed job, with the ledger at 0.2.0. One `warn` line per install is added, on distinct names too. So the degrade admits, and only the log says so. The PR body says this plainly ("judges nothing and says so at `warn`, as for the other two"). The changeset does not. No pin holds it, and none holds the other two judgements' degrade either. It is reachable only on a mismatched pair: both packages are in the changeset `fixed` group, and cloud-connection depends on the runtime at `workspace:*`. The warn says "the binder schedules none of them", which is true of a runtime that has #32563. A runtime older than #32563 keeps the later job. Fix: one case that pins the warn and the 200, and one changeset sentence.

**N3 — nit, prose, the same card.** The claim's Responsibility line asked for first-party reach to be measured, and the PR body states none. It is 0 (①).

Sentence-by-sentence agreement otherwise: the PR body's `Clause-②:` line (as far as a managed install with the switch on goes), `Metadata-protocol:` and `Skills-docs:` lines, the fix section, the refusal-versus-report section, rows 1 to 6 of the table on a deployment that runs scheduled work, the tests section, the red, green and ablation table, and the suites and verification sections. The changeset's Now, Who moves and remedy bullets and the export's paragraph match the code and the pins.

Target for S1, S2, N1, N2 and N3: one follow-up card under #31527 (`domain:server`), filed by the seat. It amends `.changeset/32572-install-local-shared-job-name.md` while the changeset is unreleased, otherwise it adds a changeset of its own. It also adds the dry-run and degrade pins. The doc half of S1 and S2 rides the jobs.mdx card the `Skills-docs:` line owes. No delta review is owed on this PR.

## Epic red-line read · 2026-11-12T23:49Z

Head-sha: `487a0f5bb8298be639a8c188039fd539c780dec7`

Verdict: **HOLD** (text only). The code passes all three red lines.

First red-line read of PR #32889 (card #32572, p2, ADR-0150).
- One must-fix, in text only: S2 below, fixed in this PR on the epic seat's ruling. After that, a text-only re-read turns this into PASS.
- One finding, F1 (a pin gap; the head itself answers right), and the contract review's S1 go to the follow-up card #32913 as nits.

Read whole: the PR body, the card and its three comments (claim 6836648648, os-dev report 6838155102, claim amendment 6838201502), the contract review r1 6838806726, the follow-up cards #32913 and #32896, the net diff against the merge base 5c0f1134 (6 files, +266 / −11), and the remerge diff of the one merge commit 487a0f5b (empty).
